newsitem.title: USA: Worst of the cold over in U.S. Midwest, Plains.
newsitem.headline: Worst of the cold over in U.S. Midwest, Plains.

text.p: Livestock producers in the U.S. Plains and Midwest may have seen the worst of the cold weather as forecasts called for temperatures to warm slightly over the weekend and early next week, meteorologists said.

"The worst is over," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. "The temperatures will still be cold today but not as cold. There are a few hints that Tuesday and Wednesday could be a few degrees above normal."
Low temperatures Friday morning fell to -32 degrees Farenheit in Aberdeen, S.D. Chicago dropped to -12 F and Indianapolis, Ind., to -8 F.

Temperatures were expected to warm into the 20s F in portions of the Midwest this weekend. Highs in the southern Plains could reach 40 to 60 degrees F, said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster for Weather Express Inc.
"Very mild conditions will be replacing the cold air," he said, referring to western Nebraska, Kansas and the Texas and Oklahoma panhandle area.
"The coldest episode on the charts is gone but by the end of next week we bring down another shot of arctic air, headed for the Midwest," Gesser added.
With the weekend warmup comes a chance for two to four inches of snow in the northern Midwest, Gesser said.
Long-range forecasts indicated another cold episode later next week but Gesser and Burgio said it did not appear to be as cold as this week's blast.
"Thursday might go colder again but we're not suggesting anything nearly as cold as it has been," Burgio said.
Gesser said that cold event would favor the eastern Iowa, Illinois and the Great Lakes region, sparing the Plains.
